en: One other extremely useful thing you can do
with Ollama, which you could also do with LM
Studio as you learned there,
is request structured data or request the
response to be structured in a certain way.
Specifically, you can ask for JSON data and
define a JSON schema to which Ollama and the
underlying model then will adhere.
So here in this example script, I again
wanna talk to the Gemma 3 model and I have a
hardcoded prompt here. And of course you
could also build an application where you
are dynamically fetching that prompt. Here
it's just hardcoded for demo purposes.
And I'm asking for a JSON list of 3
fictional users where every user should have
a first name, last name, birthdate, and
country.
And then I
again make it really clear that I want JSON
data.
And then I define a JSON schema.
And here in Python, that can be done as a
dictionary where I set up the type of the
root data object, so to say, that it should
be an array
which has 4 properties, firstName, lastName,
birthdate, country,
where every property is of type string, so a
text value where I describe every property,
which is important for the model to
understand which kind of value should go
into that property.
And that all properties are required and
must be set.
Then for the request that's about to be sent
to the model, I insert the model name, my
hardcoded prompt, and this schema under this
format parameter.
And that is something you learn in the
official docs. You can set such a format
parameter on the request you're sending to
the model.
